# Purpose and scope

This Process Characterization Plan (**PCP-003**) defines the Stage 1 (Process
Design) characterization of the A-Mab production bioreactor (Step 3), the fed-batch
cell-culture operation that establishes the N-glycosylation, charge-variant and
initial size-variant and process-impurity profile of the drug substance. The plan
specifies the objectives, the quality attributes in scope, the process parameters
and ranges to be characterized, the experimental designs, the analytical methods,
the sampling plan, the statistical-analysis approach, and the acceptance and decision
criteria by which each parameter will be classified and a design space established.

**Scope.** The `{python} f"{V['commercial_scale_l']:,}"`-L commercial-scale
production bioreactor, characterized on a qualified 2 L scale-down model (SDM).
Seed-train expansion (Steps 1–2) and harvest (Step 4) are addressed only where they
affect the production culture; their characterization is out of scope. This plan
governs execution only — the results are reported in the paired Process
Characterization Report (**PCR-003**).

**Basis.** The unit-operation model, quality-attribute framework and risk
methodology follow the A-Mab case study [@amab2009]; the Stage 1 approach and report
structure follow PDA TR 60 [@pdatr60] and the ISPE Good Practice Guide
[@ispegpg2023]; the QbD framework follows ICH Q8, Q9 and Q11
[@ichq8; @ichq9; @ichq11] and the lifecycle approach of the FDA 2011 guidance
[@fda2011].

# Objectives

The characterization will:

1. establish the quantitative relationships between the production-bioreactor
   process parameters and the cell-culture CQAs;
2. identify the significant main effects, two-factor interactions and curvature;
3. define the multivariate design space over which all CQAs are met simultaneously;
4. establish proven acceptable ranges (PARs) and confirm normal operating ranges
   (NORs) for each parameter;
5. classify each parameter for its risk of impact to CQAs and to process
   performance (CPP / WC-CPP / KPP / GPP); and
6. provide the process understanding and ranges that justify the Stage 2 operating
   conditions and the drug-substance control strategy.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis

## Unit-operation description and prior knowledge

The production bioreactor is a fed-batch mammalian cell culture operated at
`{python} f"{V['commercial_scale_l']:,}"` L working volume. It is the only upstream
operation that forms product-quality CQAs and is therefore the sole upstream step
used to define the upstream design space [@amab2009]. Platform knowledge from related
humanized IgG1 antibodies and A-Mab development experience established that Fc
glycosylation governs ADCC/CDC potency and is set in culture, that aggregate formed
in culture is polished downstream, and that the harvest HCP and DNA burden is
generated upstream and cleared by the purification train. This knowledge frames the
CQAs in scope and the prioritization of parameters for characterization.

## Quality attributes in scope

The characterization targets the CQAs set or principally controlled by the production
bioreactor (@tbl-cqa). Criticality is scored on the A-Mab continuum using Tool #1
(Risk Score = Impact × Uncertainty); attributes rated High (H) or Very High (VH) are
treated as *Critical* [@amab2009; @ichq9].

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_for(UO))
```

: CQAs in scope, with acceptance criteria and criticality (Tool #1 = Impact × Uncertainty). {#tbl-cqa}

## Risk-based prioritization of parameters

Consistent with the A-Mab lifecycle of iterative risk assessments and the risk flow
of PDA TR 60, the study scope is set by the Pre-Characterization Process Risk
Assessment (**RA-001**). A risk-ranking-and-filtering (RRF) screen scores each
parameter for its potential main-effect and interaction impact on the CQAs and
assigns the study type accordingly: parameters with a credible multivariate risk are
studied in the multivariate DoE; parameters expected to affect only process
performance are studied univariately or held at their set-point; parameters with no
credible impact over a wide range are not formally studied [@amab2009]. The resulting
parameter set and study-type assignment are given in @tbl-param.

# Materials and methods

## Scale-down model and its qualification

Characterization will be performed on a 2 L bench-scale bioreactor operated at the
commercial working-volume equivalent for pH, temperature, dissolved oxygen and CO₂
control, gas sparging, agitation power per unit volume and feeding strategy
(**SOP-2003**, **SOP-2004**). Prior to characterization the SDM will be qualified
against at-scale reference data (**SOP-1001**) by comparing the operational
parameters and, critically, the input and output quality attributes — viable cell
density, viability, titer and the glycan, charge-variant, aggregate, HCP and DNA
profiles — to confirm the model is representative and suitable to support design-space
and PAR claims [@pdatr60]. The center-point replicates of each design provide an
in-study estimate of model reproducibility (pure error) used in the lack-of-fit
assessment.

## Cell line, media and culture operation

The production culture is a fed-batch process inoculated from the N-1 seed
bioreactor at the target initial viable cell concentration, using platform basal
medium and a bolus nutrient feed (**SOP-2004**). Culture pH, temperature, dissolved
oxygen and dissolved CO₂ are controlled to set-point; osmolality is a monitored
attribute governed by feed and base addition; the culture is harvested on the nominal
duration criterion. Raw materials and media are controlled to platform specifications
and are treated as identity/quality-controlled inputs rather than characterized
variables [@amab2009].

## Analytical methods

CQAs will be measured by the validated methods in @tbl-methods; method performance
characteristics are per the cited validation reports.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(sop_table(sops=[]))
```

: Validated analytical methods for the characterization. {#tbl-methods}

## Sampling plan

Each DoE run will be sampled at harvest for the released CQAs (glycan map, charge
variants, aggregate) and for the harvest HCP and residual-DNA load; daily process
samples (viable cell density, viability, metabolites, pH/pCO₂ verification) will
confirm the culture trajectory. Center-point runs are replicated within each design
(three in screening, four in the response-surface design) to quantify reproducibility
and pure error.

## Statistical methods

Designs will be constructed and analyzed in coded factors, with each parameter's
characterization range mapped so that the set-point is 0 and the range edges are
±1 (**SOP-1002**). Screening data will be analyzed by ordinary-least-squares
regression of each response on the main effects and all two-factor interactions;
factor effects are reported as twice the coded coefficient. Response-surface data
will be analyzed with the full quadratic model (main effects, two-factor
interactions and pure-quadratic terms). Significance will be assessed at α = 0.05.
Model adequacy will be judged by R², adjusted R², predicted R² (from the PRESS
statistic), the overall model F-test, and an ANOVA lack-of-fit test against the
center-point pure error. The design space will be defined as the multivariate region
over which all CQA responses satisfy their acceptance criteria simultaneously, and
commercial-scale capability will be estimated by Monte-Carlo simulation with each
parameter varied within its NOR.

# Study design

## Factors, ranges and study type

Nine parameters are in scope (@tbl-param). The characterization range of each factor
("Range studied") defines the edges of the explored knowledge space and the basis of
the PAR; the NOR is the tighter routine-control range. Classification is an output of
the study and is reported in PCR-003. The DoE factor coding is given in @tbl-legend.

## Screening design

Factor screening will use a resolution-V two-level fractional factorial in the five
multivariate factors (A–E) with three center-point replicates, `{python} n_scr` runs
in total. At resolution V, main effects are unconfounded with one another and with
two-factor interactions, permitting clean estimation of both. Five responses will be
recorded for each run (afucosylation, galactosylation, high mannose, acidic charge
variants and aggregate). The planned coded design is given in Appendix A.

## Response-surface design

The dominant factors carried forward from screening (anticipated to be culture pH,
temperature, culture duration and dissolved CO₂) will be studied in a face-centred
central-composite design with four center-point replicates, `{python} n_rsm` runs in
total, enabling estimation of curvature in addition to main effects and interactions.
The planned coded design is given in Appendix B.

## Univariate assessment

Initial viable cell concentration will be evaluated one factor at a time across its
characterization range for its effect on peak viable cell density, titer and culture
trajectory.

# Acceptance and decision criteria

The study is acceptable when:

1. the SDM qualification confirms representativeness of commercial scale
   (**SOP-1001**);
2. the fitted response-surface models are adequate — target R² ≥ 0.90, adjusted
   R² ≥ 0.80, no significant lack of fit (p > 0.05 against the center-point pure
   error), and residual diagnostics without systematic structure; and
3. a design space exists over which every in-scope CQA is satisfied simultaneously at
   the set-point and across each parameter's NOR.

Each parameter will then be classified per the A-Mab continuum [@amab2009]:

- a parameter whose variability significantly impacts a CQA is a **CPP**; where the
  impact is reliably controlled within the design space (low risk of leaving it) the
  parameter is a **well-controlled CPP (WC-CPP)**;
- a parameter that does not significantly impact a CQA but affects process
  performance or consistency is a **KPP**; otherwise it is a **GPP**;
- consistent with the post-characterization FMEA convention, a parameter that affects
  a CQA with Severity ≥ 8, or that carries an initial (pre-mitigation) risk priority
  number > 72, is designated a CPP before mitigation by the control strategy.

The design space, classifications and PARs established here will justify the Stage 2
operating ranges and feed the drug-substance control strategy.

# Data management and integrity

All raw data, DoE designs, analytical results and statistical analyses will be
recorded and retained under the site data-integrity procedures (ALCOA+). Analyses
will be performed with version-controlled scripts and reviewed by a second analyst;
designs, models and derived design spaces will be archived with the report. Any
deviation from this plan will be documented and assessed for impact in PCR-003.

: Roles and responsibilities. {#tbl-roles}

# Deliverables and schedule

The deliverable of this plan is the Process Characterization Report (**PCR-003**),
reporting the executed designs, the significant effects, the design space, the
parameter classification and the CQA outcomes. PCR-003 rolls up into the Process
Characterization Master Report (**PCMR-001**) and provides the parameter risk basis
for the post-characterization process risk assessment. Execution follows SDM
qualification and precedes the Stage 2 PPQ campaign.

# Risks and assumptions

The plan assumes the SDM is representative of commercial scale (confirmed by
qualification) and that the platform analytical methods are validated and in control.
The principal risk is that absolute CQA values or the harvest impurity load shift at
commercial scale; this is mitigated by defining the design space on the qualified SDM,
confirming it at scale in Stage 2, and carrying the WC-CPP ranges forward with
in-process monitoring.
